memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: The Lord had said to Abram, "Go from your country, your people and your father's household to the land I will show you." - Gen 12:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God's call to Abram begins with a hard word: "Go." Leave your country, your people, your father's household - everything familiar, everything secure, everything that told Abram who he was. And go where? "To the land I will show you." Not "the land I am showing you." God does not give him a map, a destination, or a timeline. Just a command and a promise.

Notice how much Abram was asked to release. His country meant his security. His people meant his belonging. His father's household meant his identity and inheritance. God asked him to let go of all three and step into the unknown, holding nothing but God's word.

That is the shape of faith. It rarely comes with full information. God gives us enough light for the next step, and asks us to trust Him for the rest. Faith is not certainty about the details; it is confidence in the One who calls.

Hebrews says it beautifully: "By faith Abraham... obeyed and went, even though he did not know where he was going" (Heb 11:8). This is the invitation to us too - not necessarily to leave a country, but to release whatever we grip for security and follow God's leading. He may not show you the whole road. He asks only that you trust the One who sees it all.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What are you holding onto for security instead of trusting God?
- Is there a step God is asking you to take without full information?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, You call me to go without always showing me the way. Loosen my grip on what makes me feel secure, and give me the faith of Abram to trust You for the road ahead.
Amen.
